jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
THE OPPORTUNITY

We have an excellent opportunity to join a progressive Alberta school division as Director of Finance, based in Edmonton. Reporting to the Superintendent, the Director of Finance serves as the Division’s senior financial officer and leads finance administration across the organization and works directly with the Board of Trustees and its committees.

This role oversees the Division’s financial accounting, reporting, budgeting and works collaboratively with business operations in assisting in making sound business decisions. Its core areas include building the annual budget and capital plan, supporting the Board, managing contracts, agreements and partnerships.

The Division is committed to continuous improvement and continues to invest in its processes, technology and systems. This role offers real room to learn, grow and lead within an organization grounded in strong values and a deep commitment to Indigenous education. Regular travel to Division’s schools and communities is part of this role and may sometimes involve extended stays.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

The ideal candidate is a highly capable senior finance leader with a solid understanding of Board governance and the statutory and regulatory framework that school divisions work within. Progressive and motivated, this individual believes strongly in public education and in the Division’s purpose and guiding values.

The successful candidate brings a strong work ethic, a drive for excellence and continuous improvement, and a strong sense of accountability for both personal and team results. Collaborative and focused on practical solutions, this leader cares about service and has excellent organizational, technical, interpersonal and communication skills, along with the ability to resolve conflict. Equally at ease in a political setting with an elected Board of Trustees, the Director of Finance will build productive relationships with Alberta Education and Childcare, other provincial ministries and community partners.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Financial Leadership and Planning

Serving as the Division’s senior financial officer, ensuring that funding received is accurate and used according to its terms and conditions, and that operations remain fiscally sound.
Preparing financial statements, accountability reports and other required reports, coordinating the annual external audit, and making sure all legal, Ministerial and Board requirements, deadlines and Superintendent directives are met.
Directing the Division’s accounting and financial reporting, including full cycle accounting, accounts payable and accounts receivable, general ledger oversight, corporate card programs, the chart of accounts, capital and project ledgers, the fixed assets register and financial advisory support.
Direct Supervision of the Division’s financial analyst
Leading annual budget development under the Superintendent’s direction and in line with the Division’s education plan and Board guidelines, setting budget processes that meet provincial requirements and allow for stakeholder input, and preparing budget submissions, forecasts and analysis for senior administration and the Board.
Building a comprehensive budget process for every school and department, tracking grants and special project funds, and supporting principals and department heads with their budgets, grant requirements and financial affairs.
Serving as signing authority with the Board Chair and Superintendent on all financial and investing surplus funds as permitted by Board policy.
Overseeing payroll so that it reflects the Division’s values, and reviewing and approving all operating, capital and payroll expenditures as the finance officer.

Board Governance and Corporate Secretary

Co-managing all Board, committee and public meetings, with the Superintendent of Schools & CEO and the Associate Superintendent of Corporate Services. Also, from giving notice and preparing agenda packages with the Superintendent of Schools & CEO to attending meetings.
Interpreting legislation that affects Division operations, including the Education Act.
To be familiar with and apply the yearly funding manual to business operations and budget
Upholding the Board’s role as set out in Board policy, helping the Superintendent develop and review Board policy, and leading administrative procedures and policy interpretation for areas of responsibility.

Systems, Controls and Purchasing

Owning the ERP accounting platform, including data management, security, workflows and backups, and leading improvements to accounting policies, systems and processes.
Maintaining the internal audit and risk management functions
Leading the purchasing function, keeping purchasing policies and systems efficient, maintaining inventory and appraisal records, and approving changes to the vendor master.
Negotiating and co- managing tuition and transportation agreements with external partners for Board approval and making sure all contracts and partnership agreements are properly completed.

Leadership and Relationships

Leading the Division’s finance team, giving direct reports clear direction, assessing performance and developing staff through coaching, mentoring and training.
Working with Human Resources on support staff hiring, staff development and business training for school staff, and supporting the Board’s bargaining committees.
Building a strong working relationship with the Superintendent, providing the financial advice and information needed for sound decisions, and contributing to the Executive Team and its committees.
Making sure parents, staff and school leaders receive responsive service, keeping communication open and transparent, and helping resolve concerns and conflicts.
Helping build a division culture that delivers results and handles emergencies as one team, and taking on other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor’s or master’s degree in accounting, business or financial management. A CPA designation is required.
At least five (5) years of management experience, including supervising staff, managing performance and leading projects. Three (3) or more years of school division experience is an asset.
Eligibility for membership with ASBOA (Association of School Business Officials of Alberta). The ASBOA Certified School Business Official designation is an asset.
Thorough knowledge of accounting, financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, audit and financial operations.
Working knowledge of Board governance
Experience in contract management or purchasing.
Solid understanding of modern ERP and financial systems, including workflows, processes and data requirements.

KEY COMPETENCIES

Sound financial judgement, with the ability to build and manage budgets, produce financial statements and balance accounting standards, management information needs and government regulation.
Strong business sense grounded in current practices and a commitment to strategic planning, with a clear grasp of where the Division is headed over the long term and the ability to spot improvements and bring sound recommendations to the Board and the Superintendent.
Political acumen, with comfort working alongside an elected Board and other elected officials and the ability to work effectively with Alberta Education and Childcare and other provincial ministries.
Leadership that earns the trust and support of colleagues, with the ability to lead, coach and mentor a team and guide it through change.
Excellent interpersonal skills and strong written, verbal and listening skills, with the ability to work well with leaders at every level, including those from education and academic backgrounds, and to communicate clearly with staff, trustees, government officials and community members.
Creative problem solving, fresh thinking and a strong focus on service.
Strong ethics and integrity, with discretion in handling sensitive and confidential matters.

Job Description Summary

The Vice President, Sales Operations is a key member of the Canadian leadership team responsible for building and leading the operational infrastructure, insights, processes and capabilities that enable the sales organization to grow efficiently and profitably.

This role provides strategic leadership across Sales Operations functions including sales compensation, commercial analytics, pricing support, customer data, CRM effectiveness, customer implementation, sales productivity, segmentation, territory and coverage optimization, and automation.

Working closely with Sales, Finance, Marketing, IT, Customer Service, Supply Chain and other cross-functional partners, the Vice President will translate Medline Canada's commercial strategy into scalable processes, actionable insights and measurable operating disciplines. The role has particular accountability for improving sales productivity, strengthening pricing and gross margin management, optimizing sales coverage across channels, and ensuring the organization has the data and tools required to make effective commercial decisions.

Job Description

Sales Strategy, Productivity & Commercial Excellence

Partner with senior Sales and Canadian leadership to translate commercial strategy into effective sales operating models, processes, performance measures and execution plans.
Establish a comprehensive sales productivity framework, including productivity by sales channel, territory, customer segment and revenue base.
Lead sales segmentation analysis to ensure resources are aligned to the highest-value opportunities and appropriate customer segments.
Assess sales coverage and capacity across Canada, identifying areas of over- or under-coverage and opportunities to improve productivity.
Develop territory and coverage models that consider traditional field sales as well as evolving channels, particularly eCommerce and digital customer engagement.
Establish regular operating reviews that provide leadership with visibility to sales productivity, commercial performance, operational bottlenecks and emerging risks.
Partner with Sales leadership to simplify administrative work and increase customer-facing and selling time.

Sales Compensation & Performance Management

Provide executive oversight of sales compensation administration, governance and reporting.
Ensure sales compensation programs are administered accurately and on time, supported by clear service standards, controls and escalation processes.
Develop reporting that identifies sales compensation trends, exceptions and potential areas of concern.
Partner with Sales, Finance and Human Resources to ensure compensation programs support commercial strategy, desired sales behaviours and organizational priorities.
Strengthen controls, processes and automation related to compensation administration.

Commercial Analytics & Business Intelligence

Lead the Commercial Business Analyst function and establish analytics capabilities that enable faster, data-driven commercial decision-making.
Develop dashboards and reporting for sales performance, productivity, segmentation, customer revenue, pricing and gross margin.
Ensure commercial leaders have timely and consistent access to actionable business insights.
Improve bid management processes and monitor bid cycle time, quality and capacity.
Establish standardized metrics and definitions to create consistent commercial reporting across the Canadian organization.
Move reporting beyond historical results toward forward-looking insights, trends, and identification of sales opportunities and risks.

Pricing & Gross Margin Management

Provide leadership oversight for Medline Brand pricing processes and commercial pricing governance.
Establish appropriate pricing and gross margin checkpoints for large or strategically significant contracts, ensuring visibility to financial impact before commercial commitments are finalized.
Partner closely with Sales and Finance to balance revenue growth, customer competitiveness and gross margin performance.
Improve pricing efficiency through standardized approval rules, automation and exception management.
Monitor quote auto-approval, contract price activation and related pricing service measures.
Identify trends in pricing, discounts and margin performance and recommend corrective actions where appropriate.

CRM, Data & Sales Technology

Provide leadership and governance over CRM processes, adoption and effectiveness.
Ensure the CRM environment supports sales execution, pipeline visibility, forecasting and customer management without creating unnecessary administrative burden.
Establish measurable CRM adoption and process-engagement standards, including monitoring opportunity management and auto-close activity.
Lead improvements to customer and sales data quality, governance and accessibility.
Oversee customer-data processes to support timely and accurate new customer account setup.
Partner with IT and business stakeholders to integrate systems, simplify workflows and automate manual activities.

Automation & Process Improvement

Develop a Sales Operations automation roadmap focused on reducing manual activity, accelerating cycle times, improving accuracy and increasing sales productivity.
Identify high-volume or repetitive processes suitable for workflow automation, system integration or self-service.
Establish measures to quantify the productivity, capacity and financial benefits generated through automation.
Promote continuous improvement and process standardization across Sales Operations functions.

Customer Implementation

Oversee the commercial implementation process for new business and significant customer transitions.
Partner cross-functionally to identify and resolve implementation bottlenecks and improve customer onboarding.
Establish and monitor differentiated implementation cycle-time expectations for the Acute and Post-Acute businesses.
Develop reporting that highlights implementation performance by sales office, business segment and customer type.
Ensure clear ownership and escalation processes exist for complex implementations.

Leadership & Organizational Capability

Build and lead a high-performing, analytically strong Sales Operations organization.
Establish clear accountability, performance expectations and development plans across the function.
Develop talent and succession pipelines for critical Sales Operations capabilities.
Foster a culture of data-driven decision-making, continuous improvement, accountability and cross-functional partnership.
Serve as a trusted strategic advisor to Canadian Sales and executive leadership, bringing fact-based recommendations and constructive challenge to commercial decisions.
Lead change-management efforts associated with new sales processes, technology, operating models and productivity initiatives.

Key Measures of Success

Accurate and timely sales compensation administration, supported by effective controls and transparent trend reporting.
Efficient bid-cycle management and improved responsiveness to commercial opportunities.
Effective Medline Brand pricing processes, including streamlined approvals and timely contract price activation.
Timely and accurate customer account setup and strong customer-data governance.
Consistent, well-managed customer implementations across the Acute and Post-Acute businesses.
Meaningful CRM process engagement, reliable pipeline data and disciplined opportunity management.
Improved sales productivity and clear performance visibility by channel, territory, customer segment and revenue base.
Optimized sales coverage and capacity, including effective support for eCommerce and digital channels.
Appropriate pricing and gross margin governance for major contracts.
Demonstrable productivity and capacity gains generated through automation and process improvement.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Analytics, Commerce or a related discipline; an MBA or other advanced business degree is an asset.
Significant progressive experience in Sales Operations, Commercial Excellence, Revenue Operations, Finance, Commercial Analytics or a related function.
Senior leadership experience leading multiple Sales Operations or commercial support disciplines.
Demonstrated experience supporting a large, complex, multi-channel sales organization.
Strong background in sales productivity, sales compensation, commercial analytics, pricing and margin management.
Experience developing customer segmentation, territory design, coverage and capacity models.
Demonstrated success improving and automating complex commercial processes.
Experience within medical devices, healthcare distribution, pharmaceuticals, B2B distribution or another complex commercial environment is preferred.

Knowledge & Skills

Strong commercial and financial acumen, including a practical understanding of revenue, gross margin, pricing and profitability.
Advanced analytical capability with the ability to convert complex data into clear commercial recommendations.
Strong understanding of CRM platforms, sales analytics and business intelligence tools.
Demonstrated ability to develop executive-level dashboards, performance measures and operating reviews.
Strong process-improvement mindset with experience driving automation and productivity.
Excellent communication and influencing skills, with the ability to work effectively across Sales, Finance, Human Resources, Marketing, IT, Supply Chain and operational functions.
Strong change leadership and organizational capability-building skills.
Ability to balance strategic leadership with disciplined operational execution.
Demonstrated ability to lead through complexity, prioritize competing business needs and drive accountability across functions.

Leadership Profile

The successful candidate will be a commercially minded, data-driven leader who can see both the big picture and the operating mechanics behind it. They will understand how sales coverage, compensation, pricing, CRM, customer data, implementation and analytics connect to drive revenue productivity and profitable growth.

They will be comfortable challenging existing processes, using data to influence senior leaders, and moving the organization toward a more automated, scalable and insight-driven Sales Operations model.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field.
